discovery: Discovery of metal-halide perovskites as highly efficient photovoltaic semiconductors and invention of the perovskite solar cell
subfield: Condensed matter physics / materials physics of photovoltaics
motivation: In 2009 Miyasaka first used methylammonium lead halide perovskites as light absorbers in a photovoltaic cell. In 2012 Park and Snaith, working independently, made solid-state devices that were stable and efficient. Snaith also showed that the perovskite does more than sensitise: it is an ambipolar semiconductor whose charge carriers have long diffusion lengths, which made planar thin-film architectures possible. This revealed an unexpected physical property. A material processed from solution at low temperature, and full of defects, still behaves like a high-quality crystalline semiconductor, with sharp absorption edges, low non-radiative losses and defect tolerance. Within a decade, single-junction efficiencies rose above 26% and perovskite-silicon tandems exceeded 34%, beyond the limit for silicon alone. The discovery opened a new field of semiconductor physics and points to low-cost, high-efficiency solar power, a contribution of great benefit to humankind.
